findings.description: reports_archive has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored under S3's default encryption rather than an explicitly configured, auditable scheme. Notably, aws_s3_bucket_object.reports_seed_object writes into this bucket, so its contents receive no configured at-rest protection.
ledger_exports stores financial ledger exports but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data protected only by undeclared defaults and outside explicit key management.
model_artifacts has versioning and logging configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored model artifacts are not explicitly encrypted at rest.

ops_runbooks declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so operational runbooks — which commonly contain credentials, endpoints, and recovery procedures — are left without configured at-rest encryption.

This object sources resources/vendor-roster.xlsx, a vendor roster file checked into the repository that is also referenced by this configuration. Vendor rosters typically contain personal and contact data, so committing the file both embeds the data in source control history and makes it retrievable without any access control on the file itself.
